offer.say: Okay, so, every year, 12 March, one green balloon on the Mallards photo. Nobody knows who. My great-aunt says she knows and won't say. That means she knows. I want to solve it. Are you in? Say you're in.

options.text: Maybe some mysteries should stay mysteries.
I'm too busy for detective work, Tyler.

why.say: Because somebody's done a nice thing for twenty years and nobody's ever said thank you. Also because Aunt Bev knows and I don't and that's unbearable.

mystery.say: That's what Aunt Bev said! Word for word! Are you two in on it? Are you a team?

options.text: We're not a team. I'll help you look.

decline.say: Okay. I'll do it alone. Like a real detective. With a notebook. I have a notebook.

accepted.say: Start at the photo. Look at the knot. Detectives always look at the knot.

options.text: Going to look at the photo.
I've got a hunch about the bay.

p_bev.say: She'll say something mysterious. She always says something mysterious. Write it down, it'll be a clue.

complete.say: Well? Who is it? You've got a face. You've got a found-it face.

options.text: It's Earl. Every year, before anyone's in.

do.note: The Clarion, page 3: 'Mystery of the Green Balloon Solved; Icemaker Says Only Hm.'

options.text: I didn't find anything worth telling.
It's somebody who loves this rink. That's enough.

c_tell.say: EARL? Earl ties balloons? Earl! I'm telling Midge. I'm telling everyone. I'm going to say thank you to him. He's going to say 'hm'. Best 'hm' of my life.

c_keep.say: Nothing? Huh. Okay. Maybe it's a ghost. Maybe it's Gus's ghost. Gus isn't dead. A living ghost. From Florida. I'll keep looking next year.

c_vague.say: That's what Aunt Bev said too. You two are definitely a team.

done.say: Next mystery: who painted the milk bottle on board N7.
